title: Review Appointment
body:
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Getting winded easily, chesty cough every winter, forty years of smoking.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
37-year-old presenting with breathless on the stairs with a morning cough bringing up phlegm most days. Progressive exertional breathlessness with chronic productive cough and recurrent winter exacerbations. Prolonged expiratory phase with hyperinflation and reduced breath sounds throughout. Symptoms have been present for the past two years. There was a clear precipitant at onset, with partial recovery afterwards. Sleep is broken two to three times most nights. Recently relocated and registered with the practice this year.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for airflow obstruction that is incompletely reversible on post-bronchodilator spirometry. No fevers, night sweats, or unintentional weight change otherwise.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Blood pressure 110/76 mmHg, pulse 90 bpm, temperature 36.4 C, oxygen saturation 96 percent on room air. No peripheral oedema, jugular venous pressure not elevated, tar staining of the fingers. Barrel-shaped chest, hyperresonant percussion, diffusely reduced air entry with expiratory wheeze.

ASSESSMENT
Moderate airflow obstruction consistent with COPD; smoking remains the dominant driver.

PLAN
Pulmonary rehabilitation referral and smoking cessation pharmacotherapy offered. Has not tolerated a previous trial of first-line therapy. Shared decision made to reassess in three months.

Moderate persistent allergic rhinitis with a seasonal component.

title: Neurology Follow-Up
body:
REASON FOR REFERRAL
Neurology opinion for a 68-year-old. Symmetrical distal burning dysaesthesia in a stocking distribution with nocturnal exacerbation.

PATIENT-REPORTED HISTORY
The patient describes electric shooting pains in the toes and numb soles that make walking feel unsteady. The patient describes feet feel like they are on fire in bed, and I cannot feel the floor properly.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Allodynia to light touch over the dorsum of both feet with absent ankle reflexes. Length-dependent sensory polyneuropathy with reduced vibration and pinprick sensation to the mid-shin.

EXAMINATION
Monofilament sensation absent at six of ten plantar sites bilaterally, ankle jerks absent. Vibration sense reduced to the tibial tuberosity, proprioception impaired at the great toe.

IMPRESSION
Painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy with high-risk feet requiring podiatry surveillance.

RECOMMENDATIONS
Reinforce daily foot inspection and glycaemic optimisation. Patient given written information and safety-netting advice.

Length-dependent sensory polyneuropathy with reduced vibration and pinprick sensation to the mid-shin. Painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy with high-risk feet requiring podiatry surveillance.

Urgent podiatry referral for high-risk foot protection and offloading footwear. Discharged back to the referring clinician with a plan.

Left L5 radiculopathy secondary to a paracentral disc protrusion, no red flags.

body:
REASON FOR REFERRAL
General Surgery opinion for a 68-year-old. Scleral icterus with right upper quadrant colic radiating to the right scapula, provoked by fatty meals.

The patient describes intense pain below the right ribcage spreading to my shoulder blade, with jaundice and itching. The patient describes the whites of my eyes went yellow, my urine turned dark, and I get gripping pain under the right ribs.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Postprandial biliary colic with obstructive jaundice, dark urine, and pale stools. Episodic severe right hypochondrial pain lasting several hours with associated pruritus.

EXAMINATION
Tender right upper quadrant with a positive Murphy sign, scleral icterus evident, no peritonism. Afebrile, no palpable gallbladder, no organomegaly, excoriations from scratching noted.

IMPRESSION
Symptomatic cholelithiasis with choledocholithiasis causing obstructive jaundice.

RECOMMENDATIONS
Fast the patient, commence intravenous fluids, and refer for urgent ERCP. Shared decision made to reassess in three months.

title: Laboratory Interpretation

Venous blood, fasting where applicable. Collected by phlebotomy.

INTERPRETATION
Postprandial biliary colic with obstructive jaundice, dark urine, and pale stools. Biliary colic with a cholestatic liver profile; stone in the common bile duct suspected.

COMMENT
Interval laparoscopic cholecystectomy once biliary decompression is achieved. Patient given written information and safety-netting advice.

Moderate atopic dermatitis with a flare precipitated by soap contact.

Step up to a moderately potent topical corticosteroid for two weeks, then taper. No previous treatment attempted for this problem. Patient given written information and safety-netting advice.

Watery diarrhoea and vomiting since yesterday with stomach cramps and no appetite.

84-year-old presenting with watery diarrhoea and vomiting since yesterday with stomach cramps and no appetite. Acute onset watery diarrhoea with vomiting and diffuse abdominal cramping. Self-limiting gastrointestinal illness with a clear point-source exposure history. Symptoms have been present for the past year. The pattern has been intermittent with a gradual increase in frequency. Reports missing four days of work in the last month. Office-based role with a long daily commute.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for acute onset watery diarrhoea with vomiting and diffuse abdominal cramping. No fevers, night sweats, or unintentional weight change otherwise.

Blood pressure 124/93 mmHg, pulse 80 bpm, temperature 37.9 C, oxygen saturation 90 percent on room air. Mildly dry mucous membranes, abdomen soft with generalised discomfort, no guarding. No fever, no blood in the stool, observations otherwise stable.

Viral gastroenteritis with mild dehydration.

Acute otitis media with spontaneous perforation and resolving pain.

CHIEF COMPLAINT
Stiff swollen fingers and wrists every morning for over an hour, both hands the same.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
30-year-old presenting with stiff swollen fingers and wrists every morning for over an hour, both hands the same. Symmetrical inflammatory polyarthritis of the small joints with prolonged early morning stiffness. Synovitis of the metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints bilaterally. Symptoms have been present for several months. Symptoms began insidiously and have progressed since. Declines social invitations because of the symptoms. Lives with a partner and two school-age children.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for synovitis of the metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints bilaterally. Specifically denies podagra with overlying erythema and exquisite tenderness on palpation. No fevers, night sweats, or unintentional weight change otherwise.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Blood pressure 143/97 mmHg, pulse 107 bpm, temperature 38.7 C, oxygen saturation 91 percent on room air. Boggy synovial swelling of the second and third metacarpophalangeal joints bilaterally. Grip strength reduced, no deformity, no rheumatoid nodules.

ASSESSMENT
Seropositive rheumatoid arthritis, early disease, requiring prompt disease-modifying therapy.

PLAN
Urgent rheumatology referral; commence methotrexate with folic acid after baseline screening. No previous treatment attempted for this problem. Will be reviewed after the requested investigations return.

Positive for podagra with overlying erythema and exquisite tenderness on palpation. Specifically denies soft tissue injury of the lateral ligament complex without bony tenderness. No fevers, night sweats, or unintentional weight change otherwise.

Acute gout affecting the first metatarsophalangeal joint.

Standard departmental protocol. Comparison made with any available prior imaging.

title: Acute Presentation
body:
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Sudden sickness and loose stools after a family gathering, feeling drained.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
33-year-old presenting with watery diarrhoea and vomiting since yesterday with stomach cramps and no appetite. Self-limiting gastrointestinal illness with a clear point-source exposure history. Acute onset watery diarrhoea with vomiting and diffuse abdominal cramping. Symptoms have been present for nine months. Onset was abrupt and the pattern has been stable since. Relies on family for transport to appointments. Self-employed and reluctant to take time off.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for acute onset watery diarrhoea with vomiting and diffuse abdominal cramping. No fevers, night sweats, or unintentional weight change otherwise.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Blood pressure 118/80 mmHg, pulse 86 bpm, temperature 38.6 C, oxygen saturation 97 percent on room air. No fever, no blood in the stool, observations otherwise stable. Mildly dry mucous membranes, abdomen soft with generalised discomfort, no guarding.

ASSESSMENT
Viral gastroenteritis with mild dehydration.

PLAN
Exclusion from work for forty-eight hours after symptoms settle. Reports intermittently missing evening doses. Added to the nurse-led monitoring list.

title: Pathology Interpretation
body:
SPECIMEN
Venous blood, fasting where applicable. Collected by phlebotomy.

RESULTS
Electrolytes mildly deranged with a normal white cell count; stool culture negative.

INTERPRETATION
Requested for a 33-year-old with acute onset watery diarrhoea with vomiting and diffuse abdominal cramping. Viral gastroenteritis with mild dehydration.

COMMENT
Oral rehydration advice with clear escalation criteria; avoid antimotility agents. Discharged back to the referring clinician with a plan.

title: Review Appointment
body:
CHIEF COMPLAINT
The joint at the base of my toe swelled up and I cannot bear a sock on it.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
44-year-old presenting with sudden agonising pain in the big toe overnight, red hot and too sore to touch. Abrupt nocturnal onset of severe joint pain reaching peak intensity within hours. Podagra with overlying erythema and exquisite tenderness on palpation. Symptoms have been present for nine months. Symptoms began insidiously and have progressed since. Relies on family for transport to appointments. Ex-smoker with a twenty pack-year history, stopped four years ago.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for acute monoarthritis of the first metatarsophalangeal joint with florid inflammation. Specifically denies inversion injury with lateral ligament tenderness and preserved ability to weight-bear. No fevers, night sweats, or unintentional weight change otherwise.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Blood pressure 139/98 mmHg, pulse 73 bpm, temperature 38.7 C, oxygen saturation 97 percent on room air. First metatarsophalangeal joint hot, erythematous, and swollen with marked tenderness. No other joint involvement, afebrile, no tophi identified.

ASSESSMENT
Acute gout affecting the first metatarsophalangeal joint.

PLAN
Short course of an NSAID with gastric protection; rest and elevate the joint. Previous course was stopped early due to side effects. Review arranged in four weeks with the same clinician.

title: Rheumatology Follow-Up

title: Review Appointment
body:
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Cannot concentrate, no appetite, feeling worthless and exhausted.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
30-year-old presenting with flat and hopeless for months, no interest in anything, waking at four every morning. Depressive episode of moderate severity with reduced appetite and diurnal mood variation. Persistent low mood with anhedonia, early morning wakening, and impaired concentration. Symptoms have been present for eighteen months. Symptoms fluctuate but have not fully resolved between episodes. Reports missing four days of work in the last month. Works in construction with regular heavy lifting.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for persistent low mood with anhedonia, early morning wakening, and impaired concentration. Specifically denies microcytic hypochromic anaemia in the context of menorrhagia. No fevers, night sweats, or unintentional weight change otherwise.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Blood pressure 123/58 mmHg, pulse 95 bpm, temperature 38.5 C, oxygen saturation 92 percent on room air. No psychotic features, cognition grossly intact, safety plan documented. Reduced eye contact, slowed speech, mood objectively low, no active suicidal intent expressed.

ASSESSMENT
Moderate depressive episode without psychotic features; risk currently assessed as low.

PLAN
Commence an SSRI with a review at two weeks for tolerability and emergent risk. Has not tolerated a previous trial of first-line therapy. Will be reviewed after the requested investigations return.

title: Laboratory Interpretation

Requested for a 30-year-old with persistent low mood with anhedonia, early morning wakening, and impaired concentration. Depressive episode with prominent somatic symptoms; organic screen advised.

COMMENT
Commence an SSRI with a review at two weeks for tolerability and emergent risk. Advised to attend sooner if symptoms escalate.

title: Acute Presentation
body:
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Dry skin, thinning hair, low mood, and sluggish thinking for months.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
73-year-old presenting with exhausted all the time, cold when nobody else is, constipated, and gaining weight. Dry coarse skin, bradycardia, and delayed relaxation of the ankle reflexes. Insidious fatigue with cold intolerance, constipation, and weight gain despite unchanged intake. Symptoms have been present for two months. There was a clear precipitant at onset, with partial recovery afterwards. Relies on family for transport to appointments. Lives alone in a first-floor flat without a lift.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for dry coarse skin, bradycardia, and delayed relaxation of the ankle reflexes. Specifically denies depressive episode of moderate severity with reduced appetite and diurnal mood variation. No fevers, night sweats, or unintentional weight change otherwise.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Blood pressure 109/72 mmHg, pulse 110 bpm, temperature 39.0 C, oxygen saturation 90 percent on room air. Pulse 54 regular, dry skin, periorbital puffiness, no palpable goitre. Slow-relaxing ankle reflexes bilaterally, no proximal weakness.

ASSESSMENT
Primary hypothyroidism with symptom burden warranting replacement.

PLAN
Commence levothyroxine weight-based; recheck thyroid function in six weeks before adjusting. Adherence to previous therapy has been good. Advised to attend sooner if symptoms escalate.

title: Acute Presentation
body:
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Intensely itchy dry rash in the elbow creases and behind the knees, worse at night.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
86-year-old presenting with weeping cracked skin on the hands that stings with water. Flexural eczematous change with excoriation and lichenification. Chronic relapsing pruritic dermatitis on a background of personal atopy. Symptoms have been present for three weeks. Symptoms began insidiously and have progressed since. Continues to work full time but with reduced duties. Full-time carer for a relative with dementia.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for flexural eczematous change with excoriation and lichenification. Specifically denies well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scale over extensor surfaces. No fevers, night sweats, or unintentional weight change otherwise.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Blood pressure 129/94 mmHg, pulse 70 bpm, temperature 36.7 C, oxygen saturation 95 percent on room air. No secondary bacterial infection, no pustulation, skin dry throughout. Ill-defined erythema with excoriation in both antecubital fossae and popliteal fossae.

ASSESSMENT
Atopic dermatitis with sleep disturbance from nocturnal pruritus.

PLAN
Soap substitute and generous emollient; review technique and quantity used. Has not tolerated a previous trial of first-line therapy. Will be reviewed after the requested investigations return.

title: Pathology Interpretation
body:
SPECIMEN
Venous blood, fasting where applicable. Collected by phlebotomy.

RESULTS
Total IgE elevated; no evidence of secondary infection on swab.

INTERPRETATION
Requested for a 86-year-old with flexural eczematous change with excoriation and lichenification. Moderate atopic dermatitis with a flare precipitated by soap contact.

COMMENT
Soap substitute and generous emollient; review technique and quantity used. Added to the nurse-led monitoring list.
